## Purpose

This note defines an adult analysis cohort, reports missingness, and summarizes BMI and age by income group in the prepared NHANES Health Equity classroom snapshot. The summary is descriptive and unweighted.

## Load the data

```{r}
#| label: load-data
#| message: false
# Packages
library(tidyverse)
library(knitr)

# AI prompt (fallback path only): Adapt the eda03 load code for a file in
#   assignments/assignment06-eda-ai-audit/submission/, three folders below the repo root.
# Verified: From the repo root, file.exists() returned TRUE when the fallback
#   was prefixed with assignments/assignment06-eda-ai-audit/submission/.
#   The load chunk selected examples/nhanes-equity/data/nhanes_equity_v6.csv.

#Load the data
candidate_paths <- c(
  "examples/nhanes-equity/data/nhanes_equity_v6.csv",
  "../../../examples/nhanes-equity/data/nhanes_equity_v6.csv"
)
data_path <- candidate_paths[file.exists(candidate_paths)][1]
if (is.na(data_path)) {
  stop("Could not find examples/nhanes-equity/data/nhanes_equity_v6.csv")
}

#Read the data
nhanes <- read_csv(data_path, show_col_types = FALSE)
```

## Analysis cohort

The analysis cohort is adults aged 20 to 80, inclusive, in the prepared classroom dataset. Adult BMI is interpreted differently from child and teen BMI, and records above age 80 appear only in the earliest survey cycles.

```{r}
#| label: define-cohort

# Apply the cohort restriction: adults aged 20-80, inclusive
analysis_df <- nhanes |>
  filter(Age >= 20, Age <= 80)

# Flow table: N before and after each restriction
cohort_counts <- tibble(
  step = c("Prepared CSV rows", "Rows after age 20-80 restriction"),
  n = c(nrow(nhanes), nrow(analysis_df))
)

kable(cohort_counts)
```

## Missingness

Missing values were counted for each key variable within the age 20-80 cohort, before any summary. Percentages use the cohort as the denominator.

```{r}
#| label: missingness

# Key variables to check
key_vars <- c("BMI", "Age", "IncomeGroup", "Gender", "Race", "Cycle")  

# Count missing values per variable; denominator is the cohort, not the full file
missingness <- tibble(variable = key_vars) |>
  mutate(
    missing_n = vapply(analysis_df[key_vars], function(x) sum(is.na(x)), numeric(1)),
    missing_percent = round(100 * missing_n / nrow(analysis_df), 1)
  )

kable(missingness)
```

## Complete-case exclusion

Table 1 includes only records with both BMI and income group present. Records missing either were excluded after the missingness counts above were reported. The flow table shows how many records each step removed.

```{r}
#| label: complete-case

# AI prompt: Using `analysis_df` (adults 20-80):
#   1. Keep rows where BMI and IncomeGroup are both non-missing; store as `table1_df`.
#   2. Add a row "Rows after excluding missing BMI or income group" to `cohort_counts`
#      and print the updated table.
#   Use tidyverse only. Drop rows only for missing BMI or IncomeGroup, not other columns.
# Verified: table1_df has 50,851 rows; 57,137 - 50,851 = 6,286 rows dropped, matching
#   sum(is.na(analysis_df$BMI) | is.na(analysis_df$IncomeGroup)); anyNA(table1_df$BMI) is FALSE

# Keep records with both BMI and income group present
table1_df <- analysis_df |>
  filter(!is.na(BMI), !is.na(IncomeGroup))

# Add the exclusion step to the flow table
cohort_counts <- cohort_counts |>
  add_row(step = "Rows after excluding missing BMI or income group", n = nrow(table1_df))

kable(cohort_counts)
```

## Table 1

Table 1 summarizes the complete-case cohort by income group using unweighted descriptive statistics. N is the number of records in each group, and each mean and SD uses those same records.

```{r}
#| label: table1

# AI prompt: Adapt the eda03 Table 1 code to use `table1_df` instead of `analysis_df`, so N
#   counts the same records behind each mean. Remove the IncomeGroup NA filter, since
#   `table1_df` already excludes those rows. Keep the eda03 mean_sd() helper and column labels.
#   Save the table with write_csv() to assignments/assignment06-eda-ai-audit/submission/table1.csv
#   (renders run from the repo root). Use tidyverse only.
# Verified: N sums to 50,851, matching the flow table; table1_df |> count(IncomeGroup) matches N;
#   mean_sd() uses sd(), not var(); table1.csv appears in submission/ with the same three rows;
#   means and SDs recomputed by group without mean_sd() match the table

# Helper: format a variable as "mean (SD)" with one decimal (from eda03)
mean_sd <- function(x) {
  sprintf("%.1f (%.1f)", mean(x, na.rm = TRUE), sd(x, na.rm = TRUE))
}

# Summarize by income group
table1 <- table1_df |>
  group_by(IncomeGroup) |>
  summarise(
    N = n(),
    `BMI, mean (SD)` = mean_sd(BMI),
    `Age, mean (SD)` = mean_sd(Age),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

# Save Table 1 by code; full relative path because renders run from the repo root
write_csv(table1, "assignments/assignment06-eda-ai-audit/submission/table1.csv")

kable(table1)
```

## Methods note

We analyzed the prepared NHANES Health Equity classroom CSV snapshot. The cohort included records with age 20 to 80, inclusive. We summarized N, BMI mean (SD), and age mean (SD) by `IncomeGroup` using unweighted descriptive statistics. Records missing BMI or income group were excluded after the missingness counts were reported. No records were missing age. If missingness is related to BMI or income, this complete-case summary may be biased. The summary describes the prepared classroom dataset only and should not be interpreted as causal effects or population estimates.
